Please implement the Context Window Decomposition UI screen and component for the web interface in the repository at [https://github.com/HeitorM50/OsBiruBob](https://github.com/HeitorM50/OsBiruBob).

The visual design and HTML structure for this feature are already built and available in the prototipo/ directory of the repository. Before writing any React code, you must inspect the HTML and CSS files inside the prototipo/ folder. Use that prototype as the visual reference and design blueprint for the layout, component hierarchy, class names, color palette, and styling. Your task is to translate that static HTML prototype into reusable, modular React components within the existing Vite and React frontend architecture under src/ui/, wiring them to receive dynamic telemetry data from the ObserveReport context model.

The component must render the full context window token breakdown extracted during the Observe phase (Issue 8), rendering the critical overhead metrics that no default Bob IDE interface makes visible. The screen depends on the Vite and React frontend structure (Issue 41) and the demo mode file ingestion pipeline (Issue 24).

The screen must present a stacked bar visualization representing all ten breakdown sources from the context summary, ordered by token size. In addition, the screen must display three distinct top-level aggregate figures with explicit labels: fixedOverhead, conversationTokens, and reportedTotal. These three numbers must never be conflated or presented as interchangeable. Specifically, fixedOverhead represents the static system payload injected on every turn (10,439 tokens in the baseline), conversationTokens represents the ongoing conversational exchange (7,145 tokens in the baseline), and reportedTotal represents the total reported context size (17,584 tokens in the baseline).

You must adhere strictly to several core domain and visualization rules:

First, mirror the visual styling, card layouts, and bar graph presentation provided in the prototipo/ directory, adapting them cleanly into React state and props.

Second, all percentage calculations for individual breakdown sources must use fixedOverhead as their denominator. Using reportedTotal as the denominator is strictly prohibited because the ten breakdown categories account specifically for the fixed system overhead. In the baseline, toolDefinitions must clearly stand out as the largest individual slice at 5,403 tokens, representing approximately 51.8 percent of the fixed overhead.

Third, when projectRules equals zero, as is the case in the baseline, this source must be visually highlighted with an alert treatment accompanied by an explanatory message clarifying that zero means Bob IDE operated without any loaded project-specific rules or AGENTS.md instructions. When projectRules is greater than zero in subsequent runs, this alert treatment must not appear.

Fourth, all breakdown sources with a value of zero must remain explicitly visible in the legend alongside their non-zero counterparts. Hiding zero-value sources is strictly forbidden, as doing so would obscure critical diagnostic insights like projectRules being zero.

Fifth, context window pressure must only be rendered as a percentage when maxContextWindow is explicitly provided and non-null. When maxContextWindow is null or omitted, pressure must be displayed as unavailable or indisponivel, and the UI must never assume a default window size such as 270,000 tokens. When a maximum context window of 270,000 is explicitly provided with the baseline data, the pressure should compute and display as approximately 6.5 percent.

Sixth, this component must function purely as a presentation layer. It must not perform custom business classifications or re-derive raw observe logic; it simply takes the ObserveReport context data and renders it faithfully.

Seventh, the layout must be fully responsive, maintaining complete readability on mobile or narrow viewports without triggering horizontal scrolling on the page body. The visualization must meet accessibility and contrast guidelines, ensuring that segment differentiation does not rely solely on color hue by providing clear accessible labels, patterns, or tooltips.

Eighth, zero sensitive user data, private transcripts, prompt strings, or internal system paths should appear on this screen.

Explicitly out of scope for this issue are the findings list (Issue 22), the prescription interface, and the before-and-after comparison screen (Issue 23).

Write comprehensive automated frontend tests using the project test framework (such as React Testing Library and Vitest). All tests must run locally and deterministically against local fixtures. Test coverage must include:

1. Real baseline rendering with benchmark/rodada-a.json, confirming all ten sources render with correct values and percentages computed against 10,439 in alignment with the visual prototype.
2. The projectRules zero state, verifying that the visual highlight and explanation text are present.
3. A synthetic state with projectRules greater than zero, verifying that no warning highlight is rendered.
4. Missing maxContextWindow verification, confirming that context pressure displays as unavailable without numeric fallback.
5. Provided maxContextWindow verification, confirming accurate pressure calculation around 6.5 percent.
6. A zero total edge case, asserting that an empty or zero overhead payload renders safely without division by zero or NaN values on screen.
7. Responsive layout assertions checking that no horizontal overflow is introduced to the document body.

To complete the implementation, read the HTML prototype in prototipo/, inspect the ContextSummary model in docs/domain-model.md, implement the React component and its sub-elements under src/ui/ matching the prototype visual design, connect the component to the application routing and state, add the automated test suite, verify that all frontend and unit tests pass cleanly, and provide the test execution command and summary output as evidence.

# Project Instructions (AGENTS.md)

# AGENTS.md — Hindsight

Context for AI coding assistants. Keep this file short and stable.

---

## What this project is

A **static web app** (plus a dev CLI) that analyses IBM Bob session exports,
identifies context waste, generates corrected configuration — `AGENTS.md`, tools to
disable, Skills, MCPs, subagents — and compares two experiment rounds (A/B).

Pipeline: `export JSON → Parser → Observe → Diagnose → Prescribe → Compare → UI`

Everything runs **in the browser**. No backend, no database, no network calls, no
API key. A session export contains source code, absolute paths, and the commands the
user ran — it must never leave the machine. This is a hard constraint, not a
preference.

`ObserveReport` is the central contract: after F2, **no module reads the raw export**.

---

## Repository map

```
benchmark/          experiment protocol, task prompt, and both round exports
  METRICS.md        what is measured and the rules that make the comparison valid
  rodada-a.json     Round A — baseline (same as fixtures/sample-export.json)
  rodada-b.json     Round B — with generated config
  task.txt          exact benchmark prompt (character-for-character)
bob_sessions/       required screenshots of Bob sessions (submission deliverable)
docs/
  architecture.md   component responsibilities, data flow, dependency rules
  domain-model.md   all domain types with invariants (source of truth for types)
  technology-stack.md  stack decisions, commands, and justifications
  schema.md         Bob export JSON structure, field-by-field
  analise-rodada-a.md  findings from the baseline run
  ROADMAP.md        phases F0–F7, gates, and Bobcoin strategy
fixtures/
  sample-export.json  faithful copy of rodada-a.json — use for all dev/tests
data/               curated catalogues — versioned data, not code
  mcp-catalog.json    binary → MCP server (drives enable-mcp)
  tool-catalog.json   tool → purpose → group (groups unused-tool findings)
src/
  domain/types.ts   TypeScript interfaces for all domain types
  parser/           F2: validates and normalises the raw export → Session
  observe/          F2: extracts metrics from Session → ObserveReport
  diagnose/         F3: pure detectors (ObserveReport) → Finding[]
  prescribe/        F4: generates config artifacts from Finding[] + catalogues
  compare/          F5: diffs two ObserveReports → Comparison
  ui/               F6: the React SPA — this is the product
  cli.ts            F6: same core, terminal output — dev tool only
```

---

## Canonical commands

All commands run from the repository root.

```bash
npm ci                # install — use npm install only when adding a dependency
npm test              # run tests (vitest run)
npm run test:watch    # watch mode during development
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit — run before every commit
npm run dev:web       # vite — the SPA with hot reload (this is the product)
npm run build:web     # vite build → dist/web/ (static, deployable)
npm run preview       # vite preview — check the static build locally
npm run dev           # tsx src/cli.ts — CLI without building
npm run build         # tsup → dist/cli.js
npm run demo          # build + run the CLI over fixtures/sample-export.json
```

---

## Code and test conventions

- **TypeScript strict mode.** `strict: true` in tsconfig.json. No `any`.
- **One module per pipeline stage.** `parser → observe → diagnose → prescribe → compare → cli`.
  Dependencies flow downward only — see `docs/architecture.md` for the
  full prohibition list.
- **Test files alongside source.** Pattern: `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
  Fixtures go in `fixtures/`; tests import from there.
- **Pure functions for detectors.** Each detector in `src/diagnose/` is
  `(ObserveReport) => Finding[]` with no side effects.
- **No rounding in domain.** `Math.round`, `toFixed`, and truncation are
  forbidden in `src/domain/`, `src/parser/`, `src/observe/`, `src/diagnose/`,
  `src/prescribe/`, and `src/compare/`. Round only in `src/cli.ts`.
- **Timestamps are epoch milliseconds.** Type `EpochMs = number`. Never
  convert to `Date` or ISO string before the presentation layer.
- **Subtasks excluded from aggregation.** `task.parentId !== null` = subtask.
  Never add its cost/tokens to session totals (invariant I-5).
- **The core must stay browser-safe.** No Node APIs (`fs`, `path`, `process`, `os`)
  anywhere except `src/cli.ts`. The web build imports the same modules.
- **No network, ever.** No `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, telemetry — in any
  module, including the UI. The bundle is self-contained.
- **No LLM calls.** Recommendations are rule + catalogue, deterministic and traceable
  to a field in the export. Calling a model would break demo-without-API-key, static
  deploy, privacy, and explainability at once. See `docs/architecture.md`.
- **Never render export content as HTML.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`
  or `eval`. The export is untrusted input in the browser too.
- **Absence is not zero.** A metric the export does not provide goes into
  `unavailableMetrics` or stays `null` — never `0`. Estimates must be labelled as
  estimates (invariant I-6).

---

## Confirmed schema traps (read before touching parser or tests)

These bugs have been confirmed on the real export — do not re-discover them:

| Trap | Correct behaviour |
|---|---|
| `messages[].createdAt` is identical for all messages | Order by `data._meta.timestamp` |
| `_meta.spend` only exists on `assistant` messages | Guard the access — accessing it on `tool` or `user` crashes |
| One `assistant` turn can have N parallel `toolCalls[]` | Correlate by `.id`, never by position |
| `task.status` stays `"active"` after completion | Use `stop: true` on the last assistant message |
| `contextWindowBreakdown.total` ≠ `reportedTotal` | Intentional: `total` = fixed overhead, `reportedTotal` = overhead + conversation |
| `gitSha` and `gitBranch` are always `null` | Record commit SHA manually via screenshot |
| `tasks[].task.parentId !== null` = subtask | Do not double-count it in session aggregates |
| `_meta.spend` is `undefined`, not `null`, when absent | Use optional chaining: `msg.data._meta.spend?.cost` |

---

## Policy: sensitive data

**Never print, log, or copy into a generated artefact:**
- `data.content` of user or assistant messages
- `toolCalls[].arguments` (may contain file paths, commands, or code)
- `toolUsage.signature.arguments`
- `task.title` (it is the full prompt, often verbatim code)
- `task.env.staticEnvInfo.primaryWorkspace` (absolute path)

These fields are available internally for analysis but must be redacted
(`[REDACTED]`) before any output visible to the user, unless the user
explicitly enables raw display.

The `evidence.redactable` flag on a `Finding` marks which evidence fields
need redaction. Check it before rendering.

Catalogues in `data/` are the exception: they are **trusted input** (versioned and
reviewed in PR), so their text may be rendered directly.

---

## Where to implement each phase

| Phase | Files to create/modify | Input type | Output type |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F2 — Observe** | `src/parser/`, `src/observe/` | raw JSON bytes | `Session`, `ObserveReport` |
| **F3 — Diagnose** | `src/diagnose/` | `ObserveReport` | `Finding[]` |
| **F4 — Prescribe** | `src/prescribe/` | `Finding[]` | `Prescription[]`, `AGENTS.md` draft |
| **F5 — Verify** | `src/compare/` | two `ObserveReport`s | `Comparison` |
| **F6 — Interface** | `src/ui/` (product), `src/cli.ts` (dev) | all of the above | four screens / terminal output |

Each module has its own test file(s). The fixture for all tests is
`fixtures/sample-export.json` (copy of the real Round A baseline).

---

## Definition of Done (per issue)

A task is done only when:
- acceptance criteria are covered by a test or recorded evidence
- `npm test` passes
- `npm run typecheck` passes
- invalid input fails with a readable message
- no secret or private content appears in output
- the result has been verified against `benchmark/rodada-a.json` when applicable

</project_rules>

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool

You must adhere strictly to several core domain and visualization rules:

First, mirror the visual styling, card layouts, and bar graph presentation provided in the prototipo/ directory, adapting them cleanly into React state and props.

Second, all percentage calculations for individual breakdown sources must use fixedOverhead as their denominator. Using reportedTotal as the denominator is strictly prohibited because the ten breakdown categories account specifically for the fixed system overhead. In the baseline, toolDefinitions must clearly stand out as the largest individual slice at 5,403 tokens, representing approximately 51.8 percent of the fixed overhead.

Third, when projectRules equals zero, as is the case in the baseline, this source must be visually highlighted with an alert treatment accompanied by an explanatory message clarifying that zero means Bob IDE operated without any loaded project-specific rules or AGENTS.md instructions. When projectRules is greater than zero in subsequent runs, this alert treatment must not appear.

Fourth, all breakdown sources with a value of zero must remain explicitly visible in the legend alongside their non-zero counterparts. Hiding zero-value sources is strictly forbidden, as doing so would obscure critical diagnostic insights like projectRules being zero.

Fifth, context window pressure must only be rendered as a percentage when maxContextWindow is explicitly provided and non-null. When maxContextWindow is null or omitted, pressure must be displayed as unavailable or indisponivel, and the UI must never assume a default window size such as 270,000 tokens. Write comprehensive automated frontend tests using the project test framework (such as React Testing Library and Vitest). All tests must run locally and deterministically against local fixtures. Test coverage must include:

1. Real baseline rendering with benchmark/rodada-a.json, confirming all ten sources render with correct values and percentages computed against 10,439 in alignment with the visual prototype.
2. The projectRules zero state, verifying that the visual highlight and explanation text are present.

7. Responsive layout assertions checking that no horizontal overflow is introduced to the document body.

All done. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

---

## Context Window Decomposition Screen

### Files created / modified

| File | Action | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.tsx`](src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.tsx) | Created | Main React component — pure presentation layer |
| [`src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.module.css`](src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.module.css) | Created | CSS module — mirrors prototype palette and layout |
| [`src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.test.tsx`](src/ui/ContextWindowScreen.test.tsx) | Created | 47 automated tests across 8 test suites |
| [`src/ui/App.tsx`](src/ui/App.tsx) | Modified | Wired screen into the app with a demo toggle |

---

### Component architecture

The screen is broken into four focused sub-components:

- **`AggregateRow`** — the three distinct top-level figures (`fixedOverhead`, `conversationTokens`, `reportedTotal`) with the equation layout from the prototype
- **`StackedBar`** — the horizontal stacked bar with 10 pattern-differentiated segments (alternating hatch / solid patterns, so accessibility doesn't rely on color alone)
- **`ProjectRulesAlert`** — renders only when `projectRules === 0`; suppressed otherwise
- **`BreakdownTable`** — all ten sources listed with their token counts and percentages, zero values always shown, `projectRules=0` row highlighted with border and badge

---

### Domain rules enforced

1. **Percentages use `fixedOverhead` as denominator** (10,439 in baseline → `toolDefinitions` = 51.8%)
2. **`projectRules === 0` alert card** renders with `role="alert"` explaining the AGENTS.md absence
3. **`projectRules > 0` suppresses the alert** completely
4. **`maxContextWindow: null` → pressure shown as "Pressão indisponível"** — no default assumed
5. **`maxContextWindow: 270000` → pressure = 6.5%** computed and displayed
6. **Zero overhead** (`fixedOverhead = 0`) renders a fallback bar, zeroed percentages with no NaN/Infinity
7. **All ten breakdown sources always rendered** in the legend/table
8. **No sensitive data** — component receives only `ContextSummary` (no workspace paths, titles, or message content)
